title: Ge/YbF3 Defect-Cavity Dual-Band Filter with Expanded Thickness Bounds
scientific_hypothesis: Replacing ZnS/MgF2 with Ge/YbF3 material pair will resolve material_data failures while maintaining defect-cavity dual-band transmission physics. Germanium provides high index contrast in mid-IR, YbF3 provides low index with verified optical constants. Expanded thickness bounds [160,1440]nm ensure feasible initialization points.
design_principle: Single defect-cavity multilayer with alternating high/low index layers. Two defect layers positioned to create transmission peaks at 3.30 μm and 4.25 μm center wavelengths. Quarter-wave optical thickness scaling for Bragg mirrors surrounding defect cavities.
proposed_topology: Air | [Ge/YbF3]_5 | Ge_defect1 | [YbF3/Ge]_3 | YbF3_defect2 | [Ge/YbF3]_5 | CaF2 substrate. Total 20 finite layers.
design_variables: Defect layer positions fixed by topology
manufacturing_considerations: Ge and YbF3 are conventional IR dielectrics with deposition heritage
Thickness bounds [160,1440]nm expanded 20% from previous route
theory_basis: Defect-cavity resonance theory for dual-band transmission
expected_advantages: Ge/YbF3 pair has better documented IR optical constants than ZnS/MgF2
Expanded thickness bounds prevent initialization failures
known_risks: Ge has higher absorption in mid-IR than ZnS
YbF3 mechanical properties may differ from MgF2
Defect-cavity coupling may create unwanted sidebands
execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer defect-cavity dual-band filter on CaF2 substrate under air incidence. Layer sequence: Air | Ge | YbF3 | Ge | YbF3 | Ge | YbF3 | Ge | YbF3 | Ge | Ge_defect | YbF3 | Ge | YbF3 | Ge | YbF3 | Ge | YbF3_defect | Ge | YbF3 | Ge | YbF3 | CaF2. All 20 finite layer thicknesses are optimization variables with bounds [160, 1440] nm. Maximize mean transmittance in 3250-3350nm and 4200-4300nm bands. Minimize mean transmittance in 2500-3100nm and 4450-5000nm bands. Use TMM solver with NaN guards and constraint-violation logging. No metal layers. Normal incidence, unpolarized. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 2500-3100 nm, 3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm, 4450-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um bands; Low transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 24; No metal layers; Conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials only.
revision_reason: Changed material pair from ZnS/MgF2 to Ge/YbF3 to address material_data failure. Expanded thickness bounds by 20% from [200,1200]nm to [160,1440]nm per feedback directive. Maintained 20-layer defect-cavity topology.
